task_goal: Compute a group-wise behavioral-score distribution report from a table with columns apply_date (YYYYMMDD), score (numeric), group_id. Deliver two parts: (1) overall distribution per group_id -> output_1.csv; (2) monthly distribution per (group_id, apply_month=YYYYMM) -> output_2.csv. Each part reports 7 metrics: count, max, min, mode (tie -> take minimum mode), mean, median, std (sample std, ddof=1, fill 0 when n<2).

upstream_artifacts.used_for: schema expectations, known data risks, output contract, blocking-gap statement

execution_policy_for_downstream.primary: Re-run data discovery at execute time. If a data file is found, compute exactly per this plan. If still absent, emit output_1.csv and output_2.csv as HEADER-ONLY files with the exact required column order, set status='data_blocked' and rows_written=0 in the results artifact, and exit 0.

environment_constraints.implication: The implementation MUST be pure standard library (csv, statistics, collections.Counter). Do NOT plan on pandas/numpy. Consequently the plan also specifies a hand-rolled CSV reader/writer and Excel/parquet inputs are out of scope unless a library becomes available.

discovery_order: 2) any *.csv in workspace root (excluding output_1.csv, output_2.csv)
4) if multiple candidates: choose the file whose header contains all of apply_date, score, group_id; if still ambiguous, fail with an explicit error listing candidates (never guess silently)
input_contract_and_preprocessing.delimiter: sniff with csv.Sniffer, fall back to ','; strip UTF-8 BOM; tolerate CRLF
input_contract_and_preprocessing.column_validation: Validate the header (case-insensitive, strip whitespace) contains apply_date, score, group_id. Missing column -> fail loudly with a clear message. Extra columns are ignored.
apply_date_rules: read as raw string (never let a numeric loader drop leading zeros); strip whitespace and surrounding quotes
accept floats like '20240105.0' -> strip trailing '.0' first
accept 'YYYY-MM-DD', 'YYYY/MM/DD', 'YYYYMMDD HH:MM:SS' -> normalise by keeping only digits, then take first 6

result must match ^[0-9]{6}$ and represent month 01-12; rows failing this are INVALID_DATE and are excluded from output_2 (kept in output_1 is NOT allowed either -> exclude from both, and log the count)
score_rules: parse with float(); strip whitespace, thousands separators and surrounding quotes
unparseable / null / empty / inf / nan -> invalid, excluded from all 7 metrics
cnt is therefore the number of VALID score observations in the group (equals raw row count when the data is clean)
note: if invalid_score_count > 0, record both raw_rows and valid_rows in the results artifact so cnt is auditable
group_id_rules: read as raw string, strip whitespace; preserve identifier semantics (never coerce to int for the output value)
null / empty group_id -> row cannot be attributed to a group and is EXCLUDED; count it as INVALID_GROUP and report the number in the results artifact
rationale: group_id is the aggregation key; silently inventing a '__null__' bucket would misrepresent the distribution and is not requested by the spec

metric_definitions.scope: computed over the valid score values of each (group_id) or (group_id, apply_month) cell; all values are floats
metric_definitions.cnt: float(len(valid_scores)); the output column MUST be written as a float literal (e.g. '3.0', never '3')
metric_definitions.mode_score: most frequent value; Counter-based; if several values tie for the maximum frequency, take the MINIMUM of the tied values (not the first-seen one, not statistics.mode)
metric_definitions.median_score: float(statistics.median(valid_scores)); for even n the average of the two middle values
metric_definitions.std_score: float(statistics.stdev(valid_scores)) i.e. SAMPLE std with ddof=1; if n < 2 (including n == 0 and n == 1) write 0.0 — std_score must NEVER be empty/NaN
metric_definitions.empty_cell_rule: if a (group, month) cell exists but has 0 valid scores: cnt=0.0, std_score=0.0, and max/min/mode/mean/median are left EMPTY (empty CSV field), never 0

computation_steps: S1. Discover and open the input file (see input_contract_and_preprocessing); build the reader, validate/normalise the header.

S2. Stream rows once; for each row parse group_id, score, apply_date -> (group_id, apply_month, score_valid) or classify as INVALID_DATE / INVALID_SCORE / INVALID_GROUP. Accumulate per-group and per-(group, month) lists of valid scores, plus a row-audit counter set.
S3. Build the OVERALL table: for each group_id compute the 7 metrics over its valid scores; tag each record with apply_month='overall' internally (single code path shared with the monthly table).
S4. Build the MONTHLY table: same 7 metrics over each (group_id, apply_month) cell.

S5. Emit output_1.csv = overall records with the month field DROPPED (columns: group_id, cnt, max_score, min_score, mode_score, mean_score, median_score, std_score), sorted by group_id (natural/numeric-aware ascending when all group_ids are integer-like, else lexicographic).

S6. Emit output_2.csv = monthly records (columns: group_id, apply_month, cnt, max_score, min_score, mode_score, mean_score, median_score, std_score), apply_month written as a 6-char zero-padded string, sorted by group_id then apply_month ascending.

S7. Write a results artifact (analysis_results.json) with: status (ok | data_blocked), input file used, rows_read, valid_rows, invalid_date/invalid_score/invalid_group counts, groups, months, rows_written per output, and the metric definitions actually applied.
S8. Run the self-validation checklist below before finishing.

must_not_contain: an 'overall' text row in any grouping column

csv_writing.header: always written (required, including in the data-blocked case)
csv_writing.float_format: repr(float) / '%.10g' — keep full precision, do not round to fixed decimals
csv_writing.bool_bug_guard: cnt must be written via a float cast (f'{v}'), because str(3.0)='3.0' but an accidental int path would write '3'

edge_cases: n < 2 -> std_score = 0.0 (explicitly required; statistics.stdev raises StatisticsError here, so guard it)
multiple modes -> minimum of the tied modes (e.g. [1,1,5,5] -> 1.0); ties are common with integer-scaled scores, so this rule materially changes the number
all scores in a cell invalid -> cnt=0.0, metrics empty, std 0.0 (only reachable for cells created by grouping, so normally never emitted)
group_ids that are numeric-like strings: sort numerically for output readability but keep the original string in the output value
single-digit months must be zero-padded to 6 chars (202401, not 20241)
duplicate header/blank lines in the source -> skipped and counted

very large files: stream with csv.reader (no full-file load), memory grows only with the number of distinct score values held per cell (acceptable); if a single cell exceeds ~5M values, switch that cell to an online mean/std (Welford) + Counter; median then needs an external sort — document if this fallback is used because median would otherwise be memory-bound
ties in mode after float parsing (e.g. 1 vs 1.0) are the same key because scores are compared as floats
NaN/Infinity text tokens -> invalid score, excluded
validation_checklist_for_execute_node: every cnt value parses as a float AND contains a '.' (float type preserved on re-read)
std_score is never empty and never NaN (0.0 when n<2)
no 'overall' anywhere in output_2.csv; output_1.csv has no month column
row counts: len(output_1) == number of distinct valid group_id; len(output_2) == number of distinct (group_id, apply_month) pairs
reconciliation: sum(cnt in output_2 for a group) == cnt in output_1 for the same group (exactly, because months partition the valid rows of a group)
cross-check on a hand-built fixture: [1,5,1,5,3] -> mode 1.0, mean 3.0, median 3.0, std 2.0, cnt 5.0; [2.0] -> std 0.0
data-blocked case: both files exist with header only (0 data rows) and the results artifact states status='data_blocked'

open_questions: Sorting order was not specified by the task: this plan fixes group_id (then apply_month) ascending for determinism.
Treatment of rows with null group_id: this plan excludes them and reports the count (documented decision); an alternative would be a labelled '__null__' group.
Whether cnt should count raw rows or only valid-score rows: when nulls/invalids exist the two differ; this plan uses valid-score count and reports both numbers.
